summary.text: 爱 is the simplified form of 愛, used for love and affection. Its visible 友 belongs to a later graphic form; it does not show that the older graph meant “friend.”

formation.text: The history of 愛 begins with early 㤅, analyzed with 心 as a meaning element and a disputed upper sound element, identified as either 兂 or 旡. Qin-type forms add 夊, associated with walking. These accounts do not establish one complete sequence leading to 爱.

components.text: In early 㤅, 心 contributes the heart or feeling category. It belongs to 愛’s history, not to modern 爱.
The upper element in early 㤅 is identified as 兂 in one analysis and 旡 in another; both are proposed as sound elements. The competing identities remain unresolved.

sound_limitation.text: The analyses propose either 兂 or 旡 as the sound element. In modern Mandarin, 兂 is zān, 旡 is jì, and 㤅 is ài. These present-day readings do not establish which form supplied the historical sound or confirm an ancient sound match.

sound.text: The proposed 兂 and 㤅 have the modern Mandarin readings zān and ài, respectively. This comparison records their current readings; it does not demonstrate a historical sound relationship.
The proposed alternative 旡 and 㤅 have the modern Mandarin readings jì and ài, respectively. This comparison records their current readings; it does not demonstrate a historical sound relationship.

components.text: Qin-type forms of 愛 include 夊, associated with walking; the received Shuowen analysis also includes it. The accounts do not identify it as a replacement for another component.
The simplified graph visibly contains 友. It is described as replacing the lower portion of 愛 in a cursive-derived regularization; this does not establish an ancient meaning or sound role for 友.

history.text: The selected bronze-style rendering shows an early 㤅-type form; the seal-style rendering represents 愛 in the received Shuowen tradition and is associated with a Qin-type form. These are distinct graphic examples, not proof of a complete sequence.

Accounts describe early bronze forms with 心 and an upper element, and Qin-type forms with added 夊. Regional forms varied and could coexist. The earliest physical attestation and a universal sequence are unresolved.
爱 is described as a cursive-derived regularization of 愛 and was officially adopted in 1956; that adoption date does not establish when the shape first arose.

uncertainties.text: Sources disagree whether the upper element in early 㤅 was 兂 or 旡. Neither proposed sound role has a paired historical pronunciation comparison.

Early 㤅 is glossed as benevolence, while the Shuowen tradition glosses 愛 as an appearance of walking; later examples use 愛 for affection. How and when 愛 took on that affection-related use remains unresolved.

Proposed connections between the spoken word 愛 and other Sino-Tibetan words, and a separate proposal linking it with breath or inhalation vocabulary, remain disputed hypotheses about the word rather than explanations of the graph.

senses.text: A Warring States Zhongshan bronze use is cited with 㤅 in an affection-related expression. Transmitted literary examples also use 愛 for affection, but do not establish the earliest physical witness or a precise date for this sense.
愛 is used for love, affection, fondness, and liking; the evidence does not establish a dated sequence among these meanings.

limitations.text: Early 㤅 is associated with benevolence, while later examples use 愛 for affection. The transition is not securely dated, and the evidence does not settle whether it involved borrowing, replacement, or another process; no development is asserted.

overview.text: 爱 is the simplified form of 愛, used for love and affection. Its visible 友 reflects a later graphic change; it does not show that the older graph meant “friend.”

components.text: In early 㤅, 心 contributes the heart or feeling category; it belongs to 愛’s history, not modern 爱.
The upper element in early 㤅 is identified as 兂 or 旡 and proposed as a sound element; the historical comparison remains unresolved.
Qin-type and received seal-script forms of 愛 include 夊, associated with walking.
友 appears in the simplified shape after graphic regularization; it does not establish an ancient meaning or sound role.

relationships.text: In early 㤅, 心 contributes the heart or feeling category.
One analysis identifies 兂 as the proposed sound element in early 㤅; another identifies 旡. The evidence gives no historical pronunciation comparison establishing the relationship.
An alternative analysis identifies 旡 as the proposed sound element in early 㤅; the competing identification and lack of a historical pronunciation comparison leave this unsettled.
Qin-type forms add 夊, interpreted as a walking element; the Shuowen analysis also includes it in 愛.
One account describes the simplified form as replacing 愛’s lower portion with 友. The shape is also described as cursive-derived regularization, but the full pathway is not documented.
爱 is the officially adopted simplified form of 愛; its shape is described as cursive-derived regularization.
Early bronze forms of 愛 are described as 㤅, while Qin-type forms add 夊. This connects 㤅 to 愛’s graphic history without asserting a single universal lineage.
